version.changelog:
- Adds comprehensive documentation for environment-aware browser operations and backend selection.
- Details support for UI testing and credential issuance workflows, with strict user-visibility requirements.
- Documents environment detection logic for wmux, cmux, and fallback to Playwright MCP.
- Explains backend routing based on environment variables and CLI presence, including multi-var detection for cmux.
- Emphasizes that a visible browser session is mandatory when requested by the user; screenshots alone are insufficient.

llm.summary: This skill is review-worthy because it combines browser testing with broad credential discovery, token extraction, and mandatory secret persistence, even though no malware or exfiltration was found.

dimensions.detail: The stated browser-operations purpose is coherent, but the credential topic expands into checking existing secrets, issuing tokens, extracting token values, persisting them, and running downstream automation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Credential actions are framed as mandatory and automation-first, with broad trigger phrases and no consistent explicit approval gate before secret lookup, storage, or handoff.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains documentation plus one Playwright CDP helper script; no hidden installer was observed, but it instructs users to install and run Playwright tooling via npm/npx.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill reuses real logged-in browser sessions, uses CDP to pierce closed shadow roots, allows page JavaScript evaluation for diagnostics, and includes Windows recovery commands that kill Chrome processes and delete a Playwright profile.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact mandates storing issued or refreshed credentials across Vault, GitHub secrets, OS keyrings, cloud CLI configs, .env files, skill data, and keychains for later reuse.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want an agent to help manage real credentials, not just test web pages. Review every run before it reads secret stores, issues or refreshes tokens, stores credentials, modifies GitHub/Vault/cloud CLI state, or deletes browser profile data. Prefer a narrower UI-only browser skill if you do not need automated credential handling.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in context: credential-issue.md turns browser routing into a composite credential lifecycle workflow covering discovery, issuance, extraction, persistence, and automation handoff.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: the artifact mandates broad checks of skill data, project memory, .env, Vault, and GitHub secrets, plus mandatory writes to multiple secret stores and local credential files.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted: the backend is instructed to extract newly issued token values from page snapshots and persist plaintext secrets for reuse across sessions.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the trigger language mixes ordinary browser-testing phrases with high-impact credential issuance phrases, increasing accidental activation risk.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: the artifacts lack clear consent checkpoints before reading secret stores, persisting credentials, deleting browser profile data, accepting --login user:pass, or using CDP pierce:true on authenticated pages.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded: browser_evaluate can be normal for UI diagnostics, but the skill should constrain it to read-only use when it says verification must happen through UI behavior.
